newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack puts price on regulator concerns.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack puts price on regulator concerns.

text.p: Railtrack management said on Thursday that the performance payments which its industry regulator wants to review concern a scheme whereby it could earn about 280 million pounds in extra track access charges over five years from 1995 to 2000.

John Swift, head of regulator Ofrail, announced earlier that he wanted to investigate the level of performance-related income paid by Railtrack's customers, the train operating companies, following the publication of Railtrack's results earlier today.
Under the scheme Railtrack received 84 million pounds in the year to end-March 1996 and a further 84 million pounds, adjusted for inflation to 93 million pounds, in the year just ended.
Finance director Norman Broadhurst told Reuters that under the scheme it could receive a total of 280 million pounds over the full period as payments were to decline to nil by 2001.
But only about half the payments were profit since Broadhurst said Railtrack had to pay the other half out in performance payments to its own contractors.
